name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+21, one of the most Democratic seats in Georgia
Jasmine Clark holds a massive money edge: $1.6M raised and $4.2M in outside support versus no visible Chavez fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%
Open seat, with no incumbent on the ballot, adds mild uncertainty
model.rationale: The D+21 district, Clark's overwhelming financial advantage, and market pricing near 97% for Democrats leave little evidence of Republican competitiveness; the open seat is the only mild wildcard.
model.watch: Any late polling or Republican outside spending showing a far tighter race would be the main signal to revisit, though none currently exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area seat with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward Democrats. Jasmine Clark enters the general election as the clear favorite after winning the nomination, backed by about $1.6 million in fundraising and more than $4 million in outside support. Republican Jonathan Chavez shows little or no reported fundraising, leaving him with few visible resources for a general-election campaign.

No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have weighed in, so the picture rests on the district's fundamentals, the stark spending imbalance, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win near 97 percent. The open seat, with Everton Blair not on the ballot for the full term, adds a modest layer of uncertainty, but nothing in the available evidence points to a competitive race. A double-digit Democratic margin is the clear expectation.
